storage_curve.method: usable_pct = 6.7524*x + 0.07230*x^2, x = level_m - 475.5. Quadratic forced through 0 % at 475.5 m and 100 % at 488.5 m (ZRA operating band); the curvature is fitted by least squares to ZRA level/storage pairs (475.91 m = 2.89 %, 479.98 m = 31.7 %, 480.65 m = 36.68 %). Convex because lake area grows with level. Usable capacity 64.8 BCM (23.77 BCM = 36.68 % on 14 Oct 2026).

drivers_now_units.tws_cm: GRACE-FO TWS anomaly, Aug 2026, catchment mean

catchment.method: HydroBASINS level-5 basins upstream of Kariba dam (28.76E, 16.52S)

backtest.design: Strictly forward rolling origin: for each test year 2005-2026 the model is retrained on samples whose target month ended before 1 Jan of that year, then issues a forecast on the 15th of every month for h = 1..18. Target: monthly-mean usable % at t+h. Model: LightGBM (L2) on the level change, predictive distribution = median + out-of-fold residuals (leave-years-out inside the training window, same issue season); quantiles and event probabilities are read from that ensemble. Baselines refitted on the same training window: climatology (target calendar month), persistence (no change, deterministic) and ENSO-only (target-month composite for the issue-time ONI phase). Features respect publication lags (G-REALM latest pass, GRACE t-3, POWER precipitation complete months to t-1 from the daily API, root-zone wetness t-2, ONI season ending t-1).
backtest.skill_note: The full model beats climatology, persistence and ENSO-only on Brier score for the warning event at every horizon from 1 to 12 months.

no_grace_1998_2026.design: Same model without GRACE features, tested 1998-2026 (training from 1993)

crisis_2024.definition: Forecast issued on the 15th of each month; alarm probability = max P(usable < threshold) over target months Apr-Dec 2024 within 12 months of issue. 'First' = first issue month with p > 0.5.

assumptions.source: ZESCO ERB tariff application Jul 2024 (https://www.erb.org.zm/wp-content/uploads/files/ZESCO-Tarrif-Application-Submission.pdf); VoLL from developing-country literature (Vietnam 2023 implies $1.56/kWh)
assumptions.energy_conversion_note: Physics: E = rho*g*H*eta*V = 2.45 GWh per BCM per metre of head at eta=0.9; Kariba's net head is roughly 80-100 m depending on lake level -> 0.19-0.25 TWh/BCM, central 0.22. Cross-check: ~10 TWh/yr reported for both stations at the pre-drought allocations of ~45 BCM gives ~0.22 TWh/BCM. We could not source the 0.4-0.5 TWh/BCM figure and it is physically implausible at Kariba's head, so it is not used. Both banks combined; head loss as the lake falls is ignored.
assumptions.conservation_note: Conservation rate = ZRA's crisis allocation for 2024 (16 BCM/yr, cut on 28 Dec 2023).
assumptions.historical_release_note: Releases in scenario years are not published as a monthly series; we assume 30 BCM/yr spread evenly (a typical recent ZRA allocation: 2024 pre-cut and 2026 initial), and 16 BCM for 2024. Where true releases were lower (drought years), this overstates the inflow, so costs are if anything understated.
assumptions.emergency_cap_note: Emergency procurement capped at 300 MW (218 GWh/month), the replacement block costed in ZESCO's 2024 filing ($51M/month).
assumptions.terminal_credit: Storage left at end-2027 above the no-action path is credited at the contracted price (it displaces 2028 imports).
assumptions.start: Latest G-REALM level 479.92 m on 2026-11-09; scenario Nov change is pro-rated for the remaining 21 days.
assumptions.scenario_years: Hydrological years Dec(Y-1)..Dec(Y) with DJF ONI >= 0.5 (El Nino); 'all years' shown for comparison.
assumptions.scope: Both utilities (ZESCO and ZPC) and both banks; prices are Zambian (ZESCO) and are applied to both.

cost_of_waiting.method:
Cost of waiting at Lake Kariba: a deliberately simple monthly water balance.

    S[m+1] = S[m] + Q_net[m] - R[m]          (usable storage, BCM; floor 0 = 475.5 m)

Q_net (inflow minus lake evaporation) scenarios come from real historical years:
    Q_net[Y, m] = dS_observed[Y, m] + R_hist[Y] / 12
where dS_observed is the change in month-end usable storage from G-REALM levels through the
fitted storage curve and R_hist is the turbine release assumed for that historical year.

Policies compared (all start from the latest satellite level, 2026-11-09):
  * act_m      : from month m, cut releases to the conservation rate and replace the energy
                 with imports contracted in advance (17 c/kWh)
  * wait_warn  : run the plan until month-end storage falls below 20 %, then cut releases and
                 replace the energy at emergency prices (26 c/kWh)
  * no_action  : run the plan; only the floor stops it
Whenever the lake hits the minimum operating level, releases are limited to what flows in;
the lost energy is bought at emergency prices up to the emergency-procurement cap, and the
rest is unserved and priced at VoLL. Water left in the lake at the end of 2027 relative to
`no_action` is credited at the contracted import price (it displaces 2028 imports).
cost_of_waiting.headline: In El Nino inflow years, waiting from December to April adds about $16M in expected costs, and waiting until the lake crosses 20% adds about $46M ($37M if conservation starts in Dec 2026 vs $83M; $108M with no action).
cost_of_waiting.headline_note: Expected cost = mean over the historical El Nino inflow scenarios; P10/P50/P90 are across scenarios. Costs are relative to the no-action storage path (end-2027 water credited at 17 c/kWh).

limitations: Levels are G-REALM satellite altimetry (m above the EGM2008 geoid), not ZRA's gauge datum. They agree within ~0.06 m on 10 Nov 2026 (479.92 vs 479.98 m) but at the 2024 low the altimetry read ~0.2-0.4 m below the gauge (475.46-475.73 m vs 475.91 m), so near the floor usable % can be understated by a few points.
Usable storage comes from a quadratic level-storage curve fitted to five ZRA points; it is an approximation of ZRA's bathymetric table (fit error < 0.12 points at the ZRA pairs).
Satellite passes are every ~10 days with gaps of up to 60 days (marked in history_monthly as gap); monthly means use linear interpolation between passes.
The backtest uses today's versions of POWER, GRACE and ONI, not the values as first published (no vintage archive), so real-time skill may be somewhat lower.
POWER root-zone wetness shows a step change on 1 Oct 2026 (near-real-time stream); the model uses it with a 2-month lag, so the live forecast uses September 2026.
GRACE features are missing before mid-2002 and during the 2017-18 GRACE/GRACE-FO gap; LightGBM treats them as missing.
About 34 years and ~10 El Nino events: the danger event (< 10 %) is rare, so its skill estimates have wide intervals.
Releases are a policy decision; the model learns historical operating behaviour and cannot anticipate a new allocation rule (e.g. the 2027 cut to 23 BCM) except through the lake's own trajectory.
Probabilities beyond the skillful horizon mostly reflect the spread of historical outcomes for the same season.

The cost model is a transparent one-reservoir water balance: constant energy per BCM (no head effect), assumed historical releases (30 BCM/yr) to back out inflows, no spill, Zambian prices applied to both utilities.
GEOS-S2S seasonal precipitation was not used (no time to backtest it); the El Nino signal enters through ONI and the El Nino inflow scenarios.
